clean_repro.probe: POST /v2/vectordb/entities/upsert with data=[{"id": "100", "vector": [0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9]}] (string ID for Int64 PK field)

violated_assumptions: Defect assumes upsert will fail with type mismatch when string ID provided for Int64 primary key field
Defect assumes no type coercion happens in REST v2 API layer

contract_refs: No explicit constraint found requiring type rejection in upsert operations

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST v2 upsert → checkAndSetData (line 639) → json.Number(dataString).Int64() converts string to int64 → anyToColumns receives properly typed int64 value → type assertion succeeds
source_grounding.note: Source code reveals robust type coercion: checkAndSetData function (line 639-644) uses json.Number type which handles both numeric strings and actual numbers, converting them to proper Int64 before anyToColumns type assertion. The original defect claim incorrectly assumed no type conversion occurs.

falsification.probe: Query after upsert with string ID to verify actual data modification
falsification.observed: Query returns id=100 with vector=[0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9], confirming the upsert succeeded and data was actually modified - the string "100" was correctly coerced to int64 100

excluded: REST v2 API implements JSON schema coercion by design
Type coercion via json.Number is intentional API behavior

cognition_match.developer_quote: REST v2 API fails to properly serialize/deserialize complex data types - Returns wrong values for large integers, Array fields in raw protobuf format, AutoId not working for Int64 PK
cognition_match.note: This defect was filed under the historical REST v2 data type handling pattern, but source analysis shows this specific case (string to Int64 coercion) is actually handled correctly via json.Number conversion in checkAndSetData function

verdicts.rationale: The claimed defect (string ID not accepted for Int64 primary key in upsert) is FALSE_POSITIVE. Source code analysis reveals comprehensive type coercion in checkAndSetData function (utils.go:639-644) which uses json.Number(dataString).Int64() to convert string representations to int64 before type assertions. Live reproduction confirms upsert with string ID '100' succeeds and properly updates the record. The REST v2 API intentionally provides JSON schema-level type coercion as documented behavior.
